original_question: For integer sequences a1(n), ..., aℓ(n), are the following conditions equivalent: (i) the sequences are good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations; (ii) they are good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Problem 3 (Necessary and sufficient conditions for ℓ-convergence).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It identifies the correct open problem in Section 4.2 and already captures all three official conditions: ℓ-convergence for commuting transformations, ℓ-convergence for ℓ-step nilsystems, and convergence of the scalar Cesàro averages against basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequences in ℓ variables.
missing_details: The phrase "good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations" needs its full definition: for every probability space (X, X, μ), every commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1, ..., Tℓ on X, and every f1, ..., fℓ in L∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{a1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{aℓ(n)}fℓ must converge in the mean (i.e. in L2(μ)).
Condition (ii) should be made stand-alone by spelling out that it means the same L2-convergence statement as in (i), but restricted to systems that are ℓ-step nilsystems with commuting nilrotations.

The ambient nilsystem structure should be stated explicitly: X = G/Γ with G an ℓ-step nilpotent Lie group, Γ a discrete cocompact subgroup, Haar probability measure mX, and T_i x = b_i x for commuting b_i in G.

The phrase "basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence in ℓ variables" needs its definition: ψ(n1, ..., nℓ) = F(b1^{n1} ... bℓ^{nℓ} x), where X = G/Γ is an ℓ-step nilmanifold, b1, ..., bℓ commute, x is a point of X, and F is Riemann integrable.
Condition (iii) should explicitly refer to convergence of the Cesàro averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)), not to pointwise convergence of the sampled sequence ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) itself.
The draft does not state that the sequences a1, ..., aℓ are integer-valued sequences indexed by n in N.
The draft does not specify that the test functions in (i) and (ii) are bounded measurable functions, namely elements of L∞.

The nearby context in the paper indicates the author is especially interested in whether (iii), or at least (ii), implies (i); that emphasis is worth preserving in the interpretation, even though the official problem is stated as a full equivalence question.
refined_question: Let ℓ ∈ N, and let (a1(n)), ..., (aℓ(n)) be integer-valued sequences. Are the following three conditions equivalent? (i) For every probability space (X, X, μ), every commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1, ..., Tℓ : X → X, and every f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(μ), the averages A_N := (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{a1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{aℓ(n)}fℓ converge in L2(μ); (ii) the same L2-convergence statement holds whenever (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) is an ℓ-step nilsystem, meaning X = G/Γ with G an ℓ-step nilpotent Lie group, Γ discrete cocompact, μ the Haar probability measure, and T_i x = b_i x for commuting b_i ∈ G; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence in ℓ variables, i.e. every ψ of the form ψ(n1, ..., nℓ) = F(b1^{n1} ... bℓ^{nℓ}x) with X = G/Γ an ℓ-step nilmanifold, commuting b1, ..., bℓ ∈ G, x ∈ X, and F Riemann integrable on X, the scalar Cesàro averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s Section 4.2 problem on "Necessary and sufficient conditions for ℓ-convergence," not a broader neighboring question. In the current arXiv version, the exact target is Problem 3, which asks for equivalence of precisely the same three conditions. The definitions needed to make the problem stand-alone come from Section 2.4 (nilsystems and basic generalized nilsequences in ℓ variables) and Definition 3.3 (good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations for a collection of sequences). The theorem immediately preceding Problem 3 gives the analogous equivalence for the ℓ = 1 model case, while the remark and special case immediately after Problem 3 show that the author’s real emphasis is on whether condition (iii), or at least (ii), implies condition (i). Because the paper does not prove the equivalence in Problem 3, there is no paper-certified alternate formulation to return here.
